topic: Grease build-up and fire risk in kitchen exhaust systems

slides.headline: The fire starts in the filter, not the pan.
slides.subline: Grease builds up quietly, then it becomes fuel.

slides.title: Where grease collects
slides.intro: Every part of the system holds some of it.

items.title: Filters
items.text: Loaded filters stop catching, and grease moves straight into the duct.

items.title: Duct walls
items.text: A thin film on the inside is what carries a fire through the building.

items.title: Fan and motor
items.text: Grease on the blades unbalances the fan and loads the motor.

slides.note_text: Cleaning is a schedule, not a reaction to a smell.

slides.title: What a real clean covers
slides.intro: Wiping the hood is the smallest part of it.

items.title: Filters and canopy
items.text: Degreased, checked for damage, and refitted so they seal.

items.title: Duct access points
items.text: Every panel opened, scraped and cleared, not just the first length.

items.title: Fan and roof outlet
items.text: The last place anyone looks, and the first place a fire leaves from.

slides.note_text: A dated cleaning log is what an inspector asks for first.

slides.headline: Grease is a maintenance problem, not a cooking problem.
slides.subline: Book a full system clean before the season turns.

caption_en:
Most kitchen fires do not start on the hob. They start in the filter bank, where grease has been collecting for months, and then travel up a duct that nobody has opened.

Cleaning the visible hood is the easy part. The work is inside the duct, at the fan, and at the roof outlet. If your team cannot remember the last time those were opened, that is the answer.

We clean and inspect complete exhaust systems across Doha, and we tell you what actually needs replacing rather than selling a whole new system.
